arxiv-2201-05529.creator: Gerald E. Fux, Dainius Kilda, Brendon W. Lovett, Jonathan Keeling
arxiv-2201-05529.description: Abstract We introduce a general numerical method to compute dynamics and multi-time correlations of chains of quantum systems, where each system may couple strongly to a structured environment. We establish the inheritance property and invariant property of column adequate tensors.

arxiv-2406-09850.creator: Trapoom Ukarapol Tsinghua University ukarapolt10@mails.tsinghua.edu.cn, Kevin Pruvost Tsinghua University pkw23@mails.tsinghua.edu.cn
arxiv-2406-09850.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Trapoom Ukarapol Tsinghua University ukarapolt10@mails.tsinghua.edu.cn, Kevin Pruvost Tsinghua University pkw23@mails.tsinghua.edu.cn. Text-to-3D generation has shown promising results, yet common challenges such as the Multi-face Janus problem and extended generation time for high-quality assets. In this paper, we address these issues by introducing a novel three-stage training pipeline called GradeADreamer. This pipeline is capable of producing high-quality assets with a total generation time of under 30 minutes using only a single RTX 3090 GPU.

arxiv-2507-08336.creator: Zhichao Xu Zhiqi Huang Shengyao Zhuang Vivek Srikumar
arxiv-2507-08336.description: Abstract Training effective text rerankers is crucial for information retrieval. Two strategies are widely used: contrastive learning (optimizing directly on ground-truth labels) and knowledge distillation (transferring knowledge from a larger reranker). While both have been studied extensively, a clear comparison of their effectiveness for training cross-encoder rerankers under practical conditions is needed.

arxiv-2507-12915.creator: Hui Wang, Ying Wang, Xi Chen
arxiv-2507-12915.description: Abstract The population biology model holds a significant position within ecosystems. Introducing stochastic perturbations into the model can more accurately depict real biological processes. In this paper, we primarily investigate the most probable transition phenomenon in a three-dimensional nutrient-phytoplankton-zooplankton (NPZ) plankton model. With appropriate parameter values, the system coexists with a stable equilibrium point and a stable limit cycle.

pmc-11511666.title: Massively parallel measurement of protein–protein interactions by sequencing using MP3-seq
pmc-11511666.creator: Alexandr Baryshev, Alyssa La Fleur, Benjamin Groves, Cirstyn Michel, David Baker, Ajasja Ljubetič, Georg Seelig
pmc-11511666.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) regulate many cellular processes and engineered PPIs have cell and gene therapy applications. Here, we introduce massively parallel PPI measurement by sequencing (MP3-seq), an easy-to-use and highly scalable yeast two-hybrid approach for measuring PPIs. In MP3-seq, DNA barcodes are associated with specific protein pairs and barcode enrichment can be read by sequencing to provide a direct measure of interaction strength. We show that MP3-seq is highly quantitative and scales to over 100,000 interactions.
